Remiss

/rih-MISS/ - rhymes with amiss · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Remiss means negligent; careless about a duty.

Aunt Rosa never let a birthday pass unmarked, and she scolded herself as remiss if a card arrived even one day late.

Worked Example

The kennel turned Bruno away at the door. His owner had been remiss about the booster shots — two reminders ignored, an appointment made and skipped — and the kennel's rules were written for exactly such owners. Bruno spent the holiday with a neighbor, and the vaccination card came back stamped the following week.

Remiss is the exact word for that owner, because it means negligent, careless about a duty — a specific obligation existed and was let slide. Lax describes loose standards in general, a whole regime gone soft; remiss pins one neglected duty on one answerable person.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

lax: loose about rules and standards — said of regimes and rulebooks as often as people

slack: the informal word for effort gone soft

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dutiful: does every task the role demands

attentive: alert to what needs doing before being asked

Where it sits · how much damage the lapse invites — careless → remiss → reckless

careless vs. remiss: Careless is general sloppiness — crumbs on the counter, a mislaid pen — with no particular duty attached.

reckless vs. remiss: Reckless goes further than remiss — remiss lets a duty quietly slide, while reckless charges ahead in a way that courts real harm.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back

Root — miss

Root — miss: sent, let go (Latin mittere, missus)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (back) + miss (sent, let go) = sent back, let go slack. Latin remittere meant to slacken — a bowstring eased, a grip released. Someone remiss has let exactly that happen to a duty: the hold loosened, the task slid. Re- here means back — effort easing back off.

Use the root in a new word: mission

Use the root in a new word: mission: A mission is a sending — an errand you are dispatched to carry out, miss- still on the move.

Word Choice

formal / reproachful

Remiss is the courteous accusation: a specific duty existed, and it slid. It usually follows 'be' — I would be remiss, the owner was remiss — and it opens many a polite speech. Lax describes loose standards generally; remiss pins one neglected obligation on one answerable party. Among its unit-mates, recalcitrant refuses duty outright and defiantly, while the remiss simply let it slip — and reprove names the gentle correction the remiss should expect to hear.
